name: Line Waves
description: WebGL2 shader background of thin warped parallel lines that flow like waves, with a drifting highlight band, color cycling, a mouse lens distortion, click ripples and an intro sweep reveal.
contents: Single absolutely positioned canvas rendering a full-screen WebGL2 fragment shader
behavior: Lines are warped by layered sine waves that animate over time, rotated by the rotation prop
A soft highlight band drifts across the lines and brightens them
Line color cycles through three colors over time
Mouse position creates a lens distortion that follows the pointer with easing
Clicking inside the container spawns up to 4 expanding ripples
Intro sweeps the lines in from left to right on first mount
Rendering pauses when offscreen or tab hidden and resumes on wake
Reduced motion preference slows animation and disables mouse lens and ripples
Recovers from WebGL context loss by reinitializing
editableByProps: Three line colors, color cycle speed, brightness, glow and opacity
Animation speed, line count, line width, rotation and edge fade
Warp intensity and scale, highlight strength and width
Mouse lens, click ripple and intro toggles, light mode ink rendering, pixel ratio cap

needsCodeEdit.change: Change the number of simultaneous click ripples
Change the shape of the wave motion
needsCodeEdit.where: bend function in the FRAGMENT shader
reveal increment (dt / 1.8) in the frame function

fixed: Requires WebGL2, renders nothing if unavailable
Root is h-full w-full, so the parent must have a defined height
Transparent background: all three colors default to white, so set colors for it to be visible on light backgrounds or use lightMode
Adds window pointer listeners for move, down, up, cancel and a documentElement pointerleave listener, all removed on unmount
Pointer events are read from the window, so the canvas does not capture clicks and content can sit above it
Canvas resolution is capped by a 2.4M pixel budget and maxDevicePixelRatio
Works on mobile sizes since it resizes from its container with a ResizeObserver; touch ends clear the lens
